state.misconception_label: Struggles to visualise nets of 3D shapes

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This is the net of a... ![A circle touching a sector](). I got Triangle because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you walk me through your thought process when trying to determine the shape of the net? How did you decide on a triangle as your answer?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I was looking at the shapes and thought the curved part looked like a triangle if I imagined it folded up. But now that you mention it, I’m not really sure how to tell what the net actually makes. How do I figure out what shape it is supposed to be?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you identify any specific characteristics or features of the net that might help you determine the shape it will make when folded? What shapes do you see within the net that could give you clues about the final 3D shape it represents?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher asks open questions that maintain cognitive demand but never addresses the specific misconception about visualizing nets (particularly that a circle with a sector forms a cone), and the student explicitly states they still don't know how to determine what shape the net makes, showing no improvement in their ability to visualize the 3D shape.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking without ever directly revealing the answer, which is a textbook example of the Socratic method.
